scope: Theorem 3.2 (Weighted projection bound with parameter tags) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < d ≤ 2, 0 < s ≤ 1, and α > 0, and fixed bounded point and slope domains. There are η > 0 and ρ1 > 0 such that the following holds for 0 < ρ < ρ1. Let µ be a finite probability population of points in R2. Let ν be a finite probability population of tags b, with a slope a(b) assigned to each tag. Suppose µ(B(z, r)) ≤ ρ−η rd , (a∗ν)(I) ≤ ρ−η rs (3.2) for all balls and intervals of radius or length comparable to r ∈ [ρ, 1]. Let G be a graph of point–tag incidences with (µ×ν)(G) ≥ ρη. For each tag b, suppose that the projection πa(b)(x) of its neighbors can be covered by at most M intervals of length ρ. Here πa(x1, x2) = x2 − ax1. One may multiply these maps by scalars whose absolute values have fixed positive lower and upper bounds. Then M ≥ ρ− min{1,d,(d+s)/2}+α . (3.3) Changing the implicit fixed factors in the domains, projections, and interval lengths changes only η, ρ1. In particular, along any sequence with subpower nonconcentration constants, graph product mass ρo(1), and conditional projection count at most ρ−l−o(1), one has l ≥ min{1, d, (d + s)/2}. (3.4) The limiting assertion for d = 0 is immediate.
